---
title: "What are events?"
---

## Defining events in analytics

An event is a record of something that happened at a specific point in time.
Every click, transaction, sensor reading, or status change can be captured as
an event.

## Anatomy of an event

At minimum, an event has:

- **Timestamp** — when it happened
- **Type** — what kind of event (e.g., `page_view`, `purchase`, `alert`)
- **Payload** — the data associated with the event

```{r}
#| label: event-example
#| echo: true

event <- list(
  timestamp = Sys.time(),
  type = "page_view",
  payload = list(
    user_id = "u_12345",
    page = "/dashboard",
    duration_seconds = 45
  )
)

str(event)
```

## Why events matter

Traditional analytics asks "what is the current state?" Event analytics asks
"what happened, in what order, and why?" This shift unlocks temporal analysis,
funnel tracking, and real-time monitoring.
